First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time.

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 2\,\text{d}t-\int 3\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =2t-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(\frac{\pi }{2})=\pi +2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\pi +2 & =2(\frac{\pi }{2})-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+C \\ \pi +2 & =\pi -3(1)+C \\ \pi +2 & =\pi -3+C \\ C & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2t-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+5.$
